securityPage.parentRoleHelp: The role holds the capabilities and grants of every role it inherits from. Its own row rule for a table replaces theirs; without one, their rules are combined.
securityPage.standardRoleNote: Provisa's own, kept up to date by Provisa. Extend it with a role of your own that inherits from it.
securityPage.noDomainsNote: This role lists no domains, so it reaches no data. Choose the domains it may read, or All Domains, then save.
securityPage.domainsRequired: A role must list at least one domain, or All Domains. Choose its domains to save.
securityPage.noRulesMatchFilter: No rules match the current filter.
securityPage.purposeBody: A row-level security rule is a SQL predicate bound to one role and one scope. The server ANDs it into the query before execution — on reads and on writes, whichever surface the request arrives on — so a role sees only the rows its rule permits and cannot opt out by picking a different client.
securityPage.purposeAdd: Scope a rule to a single table, or to a whole domain so it covers every table in it; where both apply, the table rule wins for that table. A rule on a tag covers every table carrying the tag, now and later, and is added to the table's own rule: a tag can only narrow what a role reads. A rule is written against a role rather than a person, so what someone can see is changed by changing the role they hold.
securityPage.rolePurposeBody: A role is the unit every other permission is written against. Its capabilities decide which operations it may run, and its domain access decides which parts of the model it can reach at all. Row-level rules, and the access checks on every surface, name a role rather than a person — so what someone can see and do is changed by changing the role they hold.
securityPage.rolePurposeAdd: A role also carries its own ceilings: requests per second, and limits on query depth, node count, and execution time. That is how a role can be given reach without being given unbounded cost — an expensive query is refused by the role that issued it, not by the source it would have hit.
securityPage.ruleMissing: Before saving, choose or fill in: {{fields}}
securityPage.deleteRoleConsequence: The role is removed. A role that is still in use cannot be deleted.
securityPage.deleteRuleConsequence: Role "{{role}}" is no longer limited by this rule.
securityPage.maxQueryComplexityHint: Relations, joins, columns and nested queries of one statement, on every interface. The org limit still applies.
securityPage.inactivityDaysHint: A user's grant of this role is removed once no request has used it for this many days. Blank keeps grants until they are removed by hand.
securityPage.alsoReaches: Also reaches the domains under them: {{domains}}
securityPage.derivedRolesHelp: Derived roles: each user attribute becomes a role with no rights, such as region__eu from region = eu. Name them in masks and rules. They are never granted by hand.
securityPage.roleDescriptionHelp: What the role is for, as an access review reads it. A role that means something different in one domain is a new role there, usually a child of this one.
securityPage.ruleDescriptionHelp: What the rule is for, as an access review reads it.
securityPage.ruleDescriptionPlaceholder: Analysts read only their own region's orders
securityPage.derivedAttributeHelp: A member's value comes from their record on the Team page or, if it has none, from their identity provider's claim of the same name.
securityPage.deleteDerivedConsequence: Its roles stop being held. Masks, rules and grants that name them then reach no one.
